# secobserve_general_rule (Resource)

A rule applied to observations across every product on the instance.

~> Writing this resource requires the provider's token to belong to a **superuser** -- SecObserve rejects a general rule write from anyone else outright.

~> **Names are not reliably unique.** SecObserve's uniqueness constraint on a rule is `(product, name)`, and a general rule always has a null product; PostgreSQL treats two NULLs as distinct, so nothing stops two general rules sharing a name. Importing by name fails with an ambiguity error rather than guessing which one was meant -- import by id instead if that happens.

~> **Approval is out of band.** A rule created while general rule approval is required in the instance settings starts in `approval_status = "Needs approval"`, and every apply that touches this resource resets it back to that state. SecObserve also rejects self-approval, so the identity Terraform authenticates as can never approve a rule it just wrote -- somebody else has to do it through the UI or API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "secobserve_general_rule" "ignore_dev_dependencies" {
  name        = "Ignore dev dependencies"
  description = "Dev-only dependencies never ship, so resolve findings on them automatically"
  title       = "^dev-.*"
  new_status  = "Resolved"
}

# Rego rules run a custom policy module instead of a field match.
resource "secobserve_general_rule" "reject_critical_without_fix" {
  name        = "Reject unresolved critical findings"
  description = "Custom policy: block anything critical with no available fix"
  type        = "Rego"
  rego_module = file("${path.module}/rego/reject_critical_without_fix.rego")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Free-text description. SecObserve requires a non-empty value here.
- `name` (String) Name of the rule.

### Optional

- `description_observation` (String) Regular expression matched against the observation's description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated at all.
- `new_severity` (String) Severity to set on a matching observation. One of `Unknown`, `None`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `Critical`. The empty string leaves severity unchanged.
- `new_status` (String) Status to set on a matching observation. One of `Open`, `Affected`, `Resolved`, `Duplicate`, `False positive`, `In review`, `Not affected`, `Not security`, `Risk accepted`. The empty string leaves status unchanged.
- `new_vex_justification` (String) VEX justification to set on a matching observation. One of `component_not_present`, `vulnerable_code_not_present`, `vulnerable_code_cannot_be_controlled_by_adversary`, `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path`, `inline_mitigations_already_exist`, `code_not_present`, `code_not_reachable`, `requires_configuration`, `requires_dependency`, `requires_environment`, `protected_by_compiler`, `protected_at_runtime`, `protected_at_perimeter`, `protected_by_mitigating_control`. The empty string leaves it unchanged.
- `new_vex_remediations` (Attributes List) VEX remediations to attach to a matching observation.

~> Omit the attribute entirely to leave remediations unchanged. An empty list is **not** valid: SecObserve stores it as null, which would leave Terraform with a permanent diff, so the provider rejects it at plan time. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--new_vex_remediations))
- `origin_cloud_qualified_resource` (String) Regular expression matched against the origin cloud resource.
- `origin_component_name_version` (String) Regular expression matched against "<component name>:<version>".
- `origin_component_purl` (String) Regular expression matched against the component's package URL.
- `origin_docker_image_name_tag` (String) Regular expression matched against "<image name>:<tag>".
- `origin_endpoint_url` (String) Regular expression matched against the origin endpoint URL.
- `origin_kubernetes_qualified_resource` (String) Regular expression matched against the origin Kubernetes resource.
- `origin_service_name` (String) Regular expression matched against the origin service's name.
- `origin_source_file` (String) Regular expression matched against the origin source file path.
- `parser` (Number) Only match observations from this parser. Use the `secobserve_parser` data source to resolve a parser name to an id.
- `rego_module` (String) Rego module evaluated against each observation when `type` is `Rego`. Required when `type` is `Rego`, unused otherwise.
- `scanner_prefix` (String) Only match observations whose scanner prefix equals this.
- `title` (String) Regular expression matched against the observation's title.
- `type` (String) How the rule matches: `Fields` compares the `origin_*`/`title`/etc attributes below against each observation, `Rego` evaluates `rego_module` instead. One of `Fields`, `Rego`.

### Read-Only

- `approval_date` (String) When this rule was last approved or rejected.
- `approval_status` (String) `Needs approval`, `Approved`, `Auto approved` or `Rejected`.

~> Any create or update resets this to `Needs approval` or `Auto approved` depending on the instance and product approval settings, and reassigns `user` to whoever ran `terraform apply`. Approval itself happens outside Terraform: `PATCH .../approval/` is a separate call, and SecObserve rejects self-approval, so the identity that applied this resource can never approve the rule it just wrote.
- `approval_user` (String) Username of whoever last approved or rejected this rule.
- `approval_user_full_name` (String) Display name of `approval_user`.
- `id` (Number) Numeric id of the rule.
- `rejection_remark` (String) Reason given when this rule was last rejected, if any.
- `user` (String) Username of whoever created or last modified this rule.
- `user_full_name` (String) Display name of `user`.
